why: Treat each row as the floor of a histogram whose bar heights count the consecutive 1s ending at that row. The largest all-ones rectangle has its bottom on some row, so running Largest Rectangle in Histogram once per row solves the matrix in O(rows * cols).
hints: Fix the bottom row of the rectangle. What does the matrix look like from that row upward?
A histogram: for each column, the number of consecutive 1s ending at this row. A 0 resets the column's height to 0.
Update the heights row by row and run the monotonic-stack largest-rectangle pass on each row's heights; keep the maximum. O(rows * cols).
pitfalls: A 0 cell resets the column height to 0; it does not just stop increasing it.
Remember the 0-height sentinel at the end of each row's stack pass.
